# Fireball

Showcases burst emission, animated sprite growth, particle lights, and inherited heat-distortion particles.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Fireball)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Fireball](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/fireball.png)

## Particle System Configuration

A 1.25-second loop separates repeated explosions. The main sprites live for 0.6 seconds, leaving a quiet gap before the next burst. A spawn-triggered distortion subsystem has independent lifetime and scale, with velocity inheritance 0.5 so the heat wave can partially follow the source particle.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireball.js#L25)

```js
  const fireball = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 1.25,
    looping: true,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.2, 16, 12),
        }),
        rate: 0,
        bursts: [{ time: 0, count: 5 }],
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 0.6,
          speed: 1,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(2.5, 2.5, 2.5),
          color: [new THREE.Color('#ffffff'), new THREE.Color('#ffd166')],
          rotation: [new THREE.Vector3(-90, 0, 0), new THREE.Vector3(90, 0, 0)],
          alpha: 1,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
          radial: 0.45,
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = (0.35 + (1.8 - 0.35) * time);
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#fff2e8'),
        alpha: (time) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(time, 0, 1))),
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(fireballSprite, {
        gridSize: { x: 5, y: 4 },
        frames: 20,
        fps: 30,
        softParticleDistance: 1,
      }),
      new LightRenderer({
        count: 18,
        ratio: 0.3,
        randomDistribution: true,
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        sizeAffectsRange: true,
        alphaAffectsIntensity: true,
        brightness: 5,
        rangeMultiplier: 3,
        lightOptions: {
          color: new THREE.Color('#ffae97'),
          intensity: 1,
          distance: 8,
          decay: 2,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


[Source: system:2](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireball.js#L113)

```js
  return new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 1,
    looping: true,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Sphere(0.05, 8, 6),
        bursts: [{ time: 0, count: 5 }],
        radialSpeed: 2,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 0.5,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(6, 6, 6),
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.35, 0),
          color: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
          rotation: [
            new THREE.Vector3(-Math.PI, 0, 0),
            new THREE.Vector3(Math.PI, 0, 0),
          ],
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new VelocityOverLifetime({
        linear: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.5, 0),
      }),
      new ForceOverLifetime({
        force: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.5, 0),
      }),
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(0.55, 0.3, 0.55),
        frequency: 1.6,
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => new THREE.Vector3(2, 2, 2).multiplyScalar(Easing.cubic.out(time)),
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
      }),
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: [
          new THREE.Vector3(-0.45, 0, 0),
          new THREE.Vector3(0.45, 0, 0),
        ],
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Default, {
        alphaMap,
        softParticleDistance: 2.5,
        materialOptions: {
          opacity: 0.3,
          transmission: 1,
          distortionMap,
          distortionStrength: 0.05,
          depthWrite: false,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

The main emitter has no continuous rate: five particles burst at time zero from a radius-0.2 sphere. Their 2.5-unit scale overlaps into one explosion. The secondary burst creates five larger distortion particles lasting 0.5 seconds; radial speed 2 spreads their silhouette beyond the visible flame.

## Modules

The main scale multiplier grows from 0.35 to 1.8, making the explosion expand rather than drift. Cubic alpha decay holds brightness until late in life. Secondary upward force and noise stop the heat wave looking like a rigid expanding disc, while its cubic growth and alpha envelope independently remove the distortion.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireball.js#L50)

```js
      }),
    ],
```

## Renderers

The 5×4 atlas supplies 20 frames at 30 fps, close to the main lifetime. Soft intersections blend the explosion against geometry. Up to 18 particle lights at brightness 5 illuminate the environment briefly. The distortion material uses transmission 1, opacity 0.3, and strength 0.05; its low opacity keeps the background readable.

# Fireworks

Chained subsystems, event bursts, audio cues, particle lights, and colorful sprite-sheet fireworks.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Fireworks)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Fireworks](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/fireworks.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The 2.6-second looping rocket system owns continuous smoke and a death-triggered sparkle system. Rocket lifetime two seconds sets the burst timing. Smoke has a separate 4.5-second particle lifetime; sparkles are nonlooping with reduced gravity modifier 0.18, producing a slower downward arc after the explosion.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireworks.js#L53)

```js
  const fireworks = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 2.6,
    looping: true,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Sphere(1),
        rate: 3,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 2,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 8.5, 0),
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
          color: new Set([
            new THREE.Color('#ff4d6d'),
            new THREE.Color('#ffe14b'),
            new THREE.Color('#3eff3b'),
            new THREE.Color('#f786ff'),
            new THREE.Color('#11dfff'),
          ]),
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [],
    renderers: [
      new AudioRenderer({
        sound: [launchSound1, launchSound2],
        onDeathSound: [blastSound1, blastSound2],
        pitch: [0.8, 1.2],
        loop: false,
      }),
      new SpriteRenderer(fireworkSprite, {
        material: 'lit',
        materialOptions: {
          normalLighting: 1.0,
          sphericalNormals: 1.0,
        }
      }),
    ],
  });
```


[Source: system:2](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireworks.js#L100)

```js
  const smoke = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    gravityModifier: -0.015,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Sphere(0.1),
        rate: 36,
        radialSpeed: 0.18,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 4.5,
          speed: 0.55,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.75, 0.75, 0.75),
          color: [new THREE.Color('#4e4d4a'), new THREE.Color('#a7a097')],
          alpha: 0.1,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.75, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(0.65, 0.35, 0.65),
        frequency: 0.8,
      }),
      new LimitVelocityOverLifetime({
        limit: new THREE.Vector3(1.1, 1.35, 1.1),
        drag: 0.1,
        multiplyDragByVelocity: true,
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = (0.35 + (1.8 - 0.35) * time);
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
        alpha: (time) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(time, 0, 1))),
      }),
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: [new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, 0), new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0)],
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Default, {
        material: 'lit',
        alphaMap: smokeAlpha,
        softParticleDistance: 1,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 1,
          normalLighting: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
        }
      }),
    ],
  });
```


[Source: system:3](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireworks.js#L166)

```js
  const sparkles = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 5,
    looping: false,
    gravityModifier: 0.18,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Sphere(0.08),
        rate: 0,
        bursts: [{ time: 0, count: [100, 300] }],
        radialSpeed: [4.5, 12],
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [0.75, 1.35],
          scale: [new THREE.Vector3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), new THREE.Vector3(1, 1, 1)],
          color: new THREE.Color('#ffffff')
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
        alpha: (time) => Math.max(0, 1 - time),
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(sparklesSprite, {
        material: 'unlit',
        gridSize: { x: 5, y: 2 },
        fps: 10,
        randomStartFrame: true,
      }),
      new TrailRenderer({
        lifetime: 0.1,
        minimumVertexDistance: 0.02,
        dieWithParticles: false,
        width: (t) => 0.05 * (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(t, 0, 1))),
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        alpha: 0.5,
        textureMode: TrailTextureMode.Stretch,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 1,
          transparent: true,
          map: new THREE.TextureLoader().load(Textures.Simple),
        },
      }),
      new LightRenderer({
        count: 10,
        ratio: 0.5,
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        sizeAffectsRange: false,
        alphaAffectsIntensity: true,
        brightness: 50,
        rangeMultiplier: 5,
        lightOptions: {
          intensity: 1,
          distance: 8,
          decay: 2,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

Three rockets per second begin in a radius-one sphere with upward velocity 8.5. A discrete five-color Set gives each launch a clear color. Smoke emits at 36 per second per active context with low alpha 0.1. Each death burst creates 100–300 sparkles at radial speed 4.5–12, spreading the inherited rocket color into a broad shell.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireworks.js#L57)

```js
    emitters: [

        rate: 3,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 2,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 8.5, 0),
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
          color: new Set([
            new THREE.Color('#ff4d6d'),
            new THREE.Color('#ffe14b'),
            new THREE.Color('#3eff3b'),
            new THREE.Color('#f786ff'),
            new THREE.Color('#11dfff'),
```

## Modules

The rocket module list is empty, leaving normal integration to shape flight. Smoke uses lateral noise, velocity limits, growth, rotation, and cubic fading. Sparkles fade linearly over their 0.75–1.35-second lifetimes. Child lifetime inheritance is disabled so event particles survive after the rocket dies.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireworks.js#L77)

```js
    modules: [],
```

## Renderers

Rocket sprites are lit, with launch and death audio selected from two clips and pitch range 0.8–1.2. Smoke uses rough lit alpha sprites. Sparkles use a 5×2 animated atlas at 10 fps with random starting frames, short 0.1-second trails, and up to ten bright lights. The light cap limits a burst’s illumination cost even when hundreds of particles spawn.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/fireworks.js#L80)

# Examples

- [Additive Smoke](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/additiveSmoke.html) — Additive blending with soft particles and layered lifetime color ramps for luminous smoke. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Boids](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/boids.html) — Flocking particles using ParticleOctree aggregation, with red hazard particles acting as tagged particle affectors. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Bubbles](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/bubbles.html) — Refractive sprite transmission with spherical normals and size-driven distortion. Both continuous sounds and collision-triggered bubble pops. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Collision](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/collision.html) — Particle collision with automatic mesh detection and sorting between static and dynamic objects for optimizing octree rebuilds. Alternatively Jolt, Rapier, and Ammo can be used as external physics backends, allowing particles to affect other physics objects in the scene. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Metal Balls](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/collisionSubEmitters.html) — Collision-triggered subsystems and sound effects with physics-driven EQ filtering and live-cubemap rendering for convincing metallic surfaces. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Cube Instances](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/cubes.html) — Instanced mesh rendering with randomized cube particles and simple lifetime rotation and fade-out. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Doppler Bullet](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/dopplerBullet.html) — Doppler effect on a fast bullet particle, with smoke, faint trails, spawn blast effects, and distortion wake subsystems. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Fire](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/fire.html) — Sprite-sheet animation, soft particles, particle lights, and a heat-distortion subsystem. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Fireball](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/fireball.html) — Showcases burst emission, animated sprite growth, particle lights, and inherited heat-distortion particles. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Fireworks](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/fireworks.html) — Chained subsystems, event bursts, audio cues, particle lights, and colorful sprite-sheet fireworks. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [LOD Stress Test](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/lodStress.html) — Emitter and renderer LOD controls under a dense particle load. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Particle Trail](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/particleTrail.html) — Per-particle trail rendering with inherited color and alpha over moving particles. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Ribbon Trail](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/ribbonTrail.html) — Ribbon trail rendering for continuous streaks with lifetime fading. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Smoke](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/smoke.html) — Lit smoke sprites with soft particles and lifetime scale/color shaping. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Snow](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/snow.html) — Depth-based fading, noise-driven motion, warmup, and broad low-cost emission. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Spheres](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/spheres.html) — Lit sprite particles with spherical normals for a 3D effect. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Stylized Depth](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/stylizedDepth.html) — Depth-based color, scale, speed, rotation, and velocity modules for stylized perspective effects. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Suzanne](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/suzanne.html) — Mesh-surface emission from a model with lit sprite rendering. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Suzanne Instances](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/suzanneInstances.html) — Mesh instancing with Suzanne particles and randomized transforms. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).
- [Cubes and Spheres](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/examples/tags.html) — Tag-based module and renderer filtering by mixing cubes and spheres in one particle system. Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

# LOD Stress Test

Emitter and renderer LOD controls under a dense particle load.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=LOD%20Stress%20Test)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of LOD Stress Test](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/lodStress.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The system caps population at 50000, loops over 10 seconds, and disables gravity. This is a stress example: the cap protects against unbounded accumulation while emission and rendering LOD can reduce the actual population and visible count at distance.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/lodStress.js#L34)

```js
  const system = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    maxParticles: 50000,
    simulationSpeed: 1,
    gravity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
    gravityModifier: 0,

    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Sphere(0.7, 24, 12),
        rate: 1800,
        radialSpeed: 1.8,
        countLOD,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [2.5, 5],
          speed: [0.6, 1.8],
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.08, 0.08, 0.08),
          color: new Set([
            new THREE.Color('#57d6ff'),
            new THREE.Color('#fff176'),
            new THREE.Color('#ff6fb1'),
            new THREE.Color('#8aff8a'),
          ]),
          alpha: 0.85,
        },
      }),
    ],

    modules: [
      new VelocityOverLifetime({
        linear: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.35, 0),
        useUpdateLOD: true,
        updateLOD: moduleUpdateLOD,
      }),
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(2.5, 2.5, 2.5),
        frequency: 2.2,
        useUpdateLOD: true,
        updateLOD: moduleUpdateLOD,
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25)));
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (time) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(time, 0, 1))),
      }),
    ],

    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',
        softParticleDistance: 1,
        countLOD,
        compensateSize: true,
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

Rate 1800 with lifetime 2.5–5 would sustain roughly 6750 particles at full emission before culling. Small scale 0.08 avoids filling the screen with giant billboards. Shared countLOD starts at distance 10 with quality 0.7 and up to five levels, reducing emission workload as the camera moves away.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/lodStress.js#L43)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Sphere(0.7, 24, 12),
        rate: 1800,
        radialSpeed: 1.8,
        countLOD,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [2.5, 5],
          speed: [0.6, 1.8],
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.08, 0.08, 0.08),
          color: new Set([
            new THREE.Color('#57d6ff'),
            new THREE.Color('#fff176'),
            new THREE.Color('#ff6fb1'),
            new THREE.Color('#8aff8a'),
          ]),
          alpha: 0.85,
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

Velocity and noise use update LOD at distance 10 with quality 0.5 and one level, reducing those module updates away from the camera. Scale and alpha lifetime curves remain present to hide abrupt births and deaths. Noise strength 2.5 and frequency 2.2 make skipped motion updates visible when inspecting quality tradeoffs.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/lodStress.js#L66)

```js
    modules: [
      new VelocityOverLifetime({
        linear: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.35, 0),
        useUpdateLOD: true,
        updateLOD: moduleUpdateLOD,
      }),
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(2.5, 2.5, 2.5),
        frequency: 2.2,
        useUpdateLOD: true,
        updateLOD: moduleUpdateLOD,
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25)));
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (time) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(time, 0, 1))),
      }),
    ],
```


## Renderers

The lit Circle sprite renderer uses the same countLOD settings as the emitter. compensateSize true enlarges retained sprites to recover some coverage when fewer are drawn. This trades individual particle fidelity for apparent density. Soft-particle distance 1 reduces geometric intersections during camera movement.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/lodStress.js#L91)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',
        softParticleDistance: 1,
        countLOD,
        compensateSize: true,
      }),
    ],
```

# Particle Trail

Per-particle trail rendering with inherited color and alpha over moving particles.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Particle%20Trail)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Particle Trail](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/particleTrail.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The 2-second loop continuously feeds particles with 2.5-second lifetimes. Gravity (0, -1.5, 0) bends initially upward trajectories into arcs. Particle and trail lifetimes differ, allowing the path to linger after its source has moved on.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/particleTrail.js#L17)

```js
  const particleTrail = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 2,
    looping: true,
    gravity: new THREE.Vector3(0, -1.5, 0),
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.15, 12, 8),
        }),
        rate: 8,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 2.5,
          velocity: [
            new THREE.Vector3(-1.5, 4, -1.5),
            new THREE.Vector3(1.5, 6, 1.5),
          ],
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.15, 0.15, 0.15),
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(100, 0, 100),
        frequency: 5,
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new TrailRenderer({
        mode: TrailMode.Particle,
        ratio: 1,
        lifetime: 0.75,
        minimumVertexDistance: 0.05,
        dieWithParticles: false,
        width: 0.18,
        widthOverTrail: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
        colorOverTrail: (time) => new THREE.Color().lerpColors(
          new THREE.Color('#00d0ff'),
          new THREE.Color('#ff66ba'),
          time,
        ),
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        textureMode: TrailTextureMode.Stretch,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0.7,
          map: simpleSpriteTexture,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

Only eight particles per second are needed because their trails supply most of the visible coverage. Emission starts within a radius-0.15 sphere, with upward velocities 4–6 and lateral components between -1.5 and 1.5. The 0.15 particle scale keeps each moving source compact.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/particleTrail.js#L22)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.15, 12, 8),
        }),
        rate: 8,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 2.5,
          velocity: [
            new THREE.Vector3(-1.5, 4, -1.5),
            new THREE.Vector3(1.5, 6, 1.5),
          ],
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.15, 0.15, 0.15),
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

TransformByNoise uses strong horizontal components (100) and zero vertical strength at frequency 5. The result strongly perturbs the lateral path while gravity and initial vertical velocity still shape its height. The large strength is a visible parameter to inspect carefully when adapting the effect to another scene scale.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/particleTrail.js#L40)

```js
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(100, 0, 100),
        frequency: 5,
      }),
    ],
```


## Renderers

Particle mode gives every selected particle its own trail, with ratio 1. Trail lifetime 0.75 and minimum vertex distance 0.05 balance persistence against vertex count. Width 0.18 tapers at both ends; the cyan-to-pink gradient makes progression along the path readable. dieWithParticles false lets older trail segments finish fading.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/particleTrail.js#L48)

```js
    renderers: [
      new TrailRenderer({
        mode: TrailMode.Particle,
        ratio: 1,
        lifetime: 0.75,
        minimumVertexDistance: 0.05,
        dieWithParticles: false,
        width: 0.18,
        widthOverTrail: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
        colorOverTrail: (time) => new THREE.Color().lerpColors(
          new THREE.Color('#00d0ff'),
          new THREE.Color('#ff66ba'),
          time,
        ),
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        textureMode: TrailTextureMode.Stretch,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0.7,
          map: simpleSpriteTexture,
        },
      }),
    ],
```

<!-- Source: apps/docs/examples/ribbonTrail.md -->


# Ribbon Trail

Ribbon trail rendering for continuous streaks with lifetime fading.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Ribbon%20Trail)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Ribbon Trail](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/ribbonTrail.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The 4-second loop supplies a continuous ribbon field. Each particle lasts one second, so its contribution remains near the current emitter rather than accumulating indefinitely. No gravity override is supplied; the system’s default gravity behavior still applies.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/ribbonTrail.js#L13)

```js
  const ribbonTrail = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 4,
    looping: true,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Torus(),
        rate: 50,
        radialSpeed: 5,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 1,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.12, 0.12, 0.12),
        },
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new TrailRenderer({
        mode: TrailMode.Ribbon,
        ratio: 1,
        ribbonCount: 3,
        width: 0.15,
        widthOverTrail: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
        colorOverTrail: (time) => new THREE.Color().lerpColors(
          new THREE.Color('#fff'),
          new THREE.Color('#66e0ff'),
          time,
        ),
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0,
          metalness: 0,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

The torus source emits 50 particles per second with radial speed 5. A short one-second lifetime and scale 0.12 produce many closely spaced samples around the source. Increasing speed without increasing emission rate would separate those samples and visibly change the ribbon shape.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/ribbonTrail.js#L18)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Torus(),
        rate: 50,
        radialSpeed: 5,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 1,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.12, 0.12, 0.12),
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

No module array is supplied here; the system therefore uses its empty module default. The system configuration shown below is the actual source for that absence. Motion comes from initial radial velocity and default system integration, while width and color variation are handled by the trail renderer.


[Source: modules:none](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/ribbonTrail.js#L14)

```js
  const ribbonTrail = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 4,
    looping: true,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: EmissionShape.Torus(),
        rate: 50,
        radialSpeed: 5,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 1,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.12, 0.12, 0.12),
        },
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new TrailRenderer({
        mode: TrailMode.Ribbon,
        ratio: 1,
        ribbonCount: 3,
        width: 0.15,
        widthOverTrail: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
        colorOverTrail: (time) => new THREE.Color().lerpColors(
          new THREE.Color('#fff'),
          new THREE.Color('#66e0ff'),
          time,
        ),
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0,
          metalness: 0,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Renderers

Ribbon mode connects particles into three ribbons rather than assigning an independent trail to each particle. Ratio 1 includes all samples and width 0.15 keeps the strands narrow. The width envelope tapers both ends and the white-to-cyan gradient distinguishes the length of the ribbon. Roughness and metalness zero create a clean nonmetallic surface response.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/ribbonTrail.js#L31)

```js
    renderers: [
      new TrailRenderer({
        mode: TrailMode.Ribbon,
        ratio: 1,
        ribbonCount: 3,
        width: 0.15,
        widthOverTrail: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
        colorOverTrail: (time) => new THREE.Color().lerpColors(
          new THREE.Color('#fff'),
          new THREE.Color('#66e0ff'),
          time,
        ),
        inheritParticleColor: true,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0,
          metalness: 0,
        },
      }),
    ],
```

<!-- Source: apps/docs/examples/smoke.md -->


# Smoke

Lit smoke sprites with soft particles and lifetime scale/color shaping.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Smoke)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Smoke](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/smoke.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The 10-second loop sustains a plume while particles live for 4.5 seconds. The small negative gravity modifier reverses the default downward acceleration, adding slow buoyancy. Long particle lifetimes let the plume accumulate and spread instead of looking like short flame tongues.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/smoke.js#L18)

```js
  const smoke = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    gravityModifier: -0.015,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.75, 1.2, 24),
        }),
        rate: 36,
        radialSpeed: 0.18,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 4.5,
          speed: 0.55,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(2.5, 2.5, 2.5),
          color: [new THREE.Color('#4e4d4a'), new THREE.Color('#a7a097')],
          alpha: 0.55,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.75, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(0.65, 0.35, 0.65),
        frequency: 0.8,
      }),
      new LimitVelocityOverLifetime({
        limit: new THREE.Vector3(1.1, 1.35, 1.1),
        drag: 0.1,
        multiplyDragByVelocity: true,
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = (0.35 + (1.8 - 0.35) * time);
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
        alpha: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
      }),
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: [new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, 0), new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0)],
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Default, {
        material: 'lit',
        alphaMap: smokeAlpha,
        softParticleDistance: 1,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 1,
          normalLighting: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
        }
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

A cone of radius 0.75 and height 1.2 provides a broad source. Rate 36 and lifetime 4.5 imply about 162 live particles at steady emission. Upward velocity 0.75 and radial speed 0.18 favor a column with modest spread. Scale 2.5 overlaps the low-opacity, alpha-0.55 sprites into a continuous volume.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/smoke.js#L23)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.75, 1.2, 24),
        }),
        rate: 36,
        radialSpeed: 0.18,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 4.5,
          speed: 0.55,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(2.5, 2.5, 2.5),
          color: [new THREE.Color('#4e4d4a'), new THREE.Color('#a7a097')],
          alpha: 0.55,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.75, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

Noise is stronger horizontally (0.65) than vertically (0.35), producing rolling lateral motion. Velocity limits and drag prevent indefinite acceleration. The scale multiplier grows from 0.35 to 1.8, representing dispersal, and the alpha curve hides the first fifth and final quarter of the lifetime. Random angular velocity breaks up repeated texture orientation.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/smoke.js#L42)

```js
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(0.65, 0.35, 0.65),
        frequency: 0.8,
      }),
      new LimitVelocityOverLifetime({
        limit: new THREE.Vector3(1.1, 1.35, 1.1),
        drag: 0.1,
        multiplyDragByVelocity: true,
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = (0.35 + (1.8 - 0.35) * time);
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
        alpha: (time) => ((time) < 0.2 ? (time) / 0.2 : (time) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((time) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((time) - 0.75) / 0.25))),
      }),
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: [new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, 0), new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0)],
      }),
    ],
```


## Renderers

Lit sprites use the smoke alpha image as their silhouette. Roughness 1 avoids glossy highlights; spherical normals 1 and normal lighting 0.5 give each billboard some volume under scene lighting. Soft-particle distance 1 reduces hard lines where the smoke intersects geometry.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/smoke.js#L68)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Default, {
        material: 'lit',
        alphaMap: smokeAlpha,
        softParticleDistance: 1,
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 1,
          normalLighting: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
        }
      }),
    ],
```

# Snow

Depth-based fading, noise-driven motion, warmup, and broad low-cost emission.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Snow)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Snow](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/snow.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The snow is positioned five units above the origin. A 10-second loop with prewarm fills the scene before the ordinary demo begins; the preview CLI instead uses its explicit warmup count. Gravity modifier 0.025 gives a slow fall over the long 16-second particle lifetime.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/snow.js#L18)

```js
  const snow = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    prewarm: true,
    looping: true,
    gravityModifier: 0.025,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.BoxGeometry(30, 0.1, 30),
        }),
        rate: 200,
        radialSpeed: 0,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 16,
          speed: 1,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
          color: new THREE.Color('#e9f7ff'),
          alpha: 0.9,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, -0.35, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(0.28, 0.02, 0.28),
        frequency: 0.55,
      }),
      new LimitVelocityOverLifetime({
        limit: new THREE.Vector3(0.7, 0.65, 0.7),
        drag: 0.12,
        multiplyDragByVelocity: true,
      }),
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: new THREE.Vector3(0.65, 0, 0),
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (t) => ((t) < 0.2 ? (t) / 0.2 : (t) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((t) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((t) - 0.75) / 0.25)))
      }),
      new ColorByDepth({
        alpha: [1, 0.5],
        depthRange: [6, 24],
      }),
      new ColorByDepth({
        alpha: [0, 1],
        depthRange: [1, 2],
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Default, {
        material: 'lit',
        alphaMap: snowflakeAlpha,
        materialOptions: {
          normalLighting: 0.25,
          sphericalNormals: 0.1
        }
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

A 30×0.1×30 box distributes snow across a wide area. Rate 200 can sustain about 3200 particles at full lifetime, so the 0.25-unit flakes remain individually small. Radial speed is zero and initial vertical velocity is -0.35, avoiding an outward blast from the box.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/snow.js#L24)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.BoxGeometry(30, 0.1, 30),
        }),
        rate: 200,
        radialSpeed: 0,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 16,
          speed: 1,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
          color: new THREE.Color('#e9f7ff'),
          alpha: 0.9,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, -0.35, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

Horizontal noise strength 0.28 and vertical strength 0.02 create drifting flakes. Velocity limits and drag prevent rapid falling. A small constant rotation animates the snow silhouette. Depth fades reduce distant alpha between depths 6 and 24 and remove flakes very near the camera between depths 1 and 2; the lifetime envelope softens population turnover.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/snow.js#L43)

```js
    modules: [
      new TransformByNoise({
        strength: new THREE.Vector3(0.28, 0.02, 0.28),
        frequency: 0.55,
      }),
      new LimitVelocityOverLifetime({
        limit: new THREE.Vector3(0.7, 0.65, 0.7),
        drag: 0.12,
        multiplyDragByVelocity: true,
      }),
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: new THREE.Vector3(0.65, 0, 0),
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (t) => ((t) < 0.2 ? (t) / 0.2 : (t) < 0.75 ? 1 - 0.15 * (((t) - 0.2) / 0.55) : 0.85 * (1 - (((t) - 0.75) / 0.25)))
      }),
      new ColorByDepth({
        alpha: [1, 0.5],
        depthRange: [6, 24],
      }),
      new ColorByDepth({
        alpha: [0, 1],
        depthRange: [1, 2],
      }),
    ],
```


## Renderers

The snowflake alpha texture provides detail using one lit billboard per particle. Normal lighting 0.25 and spherical normals 0.1 keep shading subtle instead of making flakes look like balls. This is less geometric work than individually modeled snowflakes at the same population.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/snow.js#L70)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Default, {
        material: 'lit',
        alphaMap: snowflakeAlpha,
        materialOptions: {
          normalLighting: 0.25,
          sphericalNormals: 0.1
        }
      }),
    ],
```

# Spheres

Lit sprite particles with spherical normals for a 3D effect.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Spheres)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Spheres](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/spheres.png)

## Particle System Configuration

This 10-second looping system has zero gravity and no gravity modifier, so the particles show simple outward movement without falling. Lifetimes of 6–12 seconds keep particles visible long enough to inspect the lighting illusion as they spread.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/spheres.js#L18)

```js
  const system = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    gravity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
    gravityModifier: 0,

    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        rate: 12,
        radialSpeed: 1,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [6, 12],
          speed: 1,
          color: colors,
          scale: [
            new THREE.Vector3(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
            new THREE.Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
          ],
          alpha: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],

    modules: [],

    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',

        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
          normalLighting: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

Rate 12 and mean lifetime 9 imply roughly 108 live particles before culling. A discrete four-color Set keeps recognizable red, green, yellow, and blue groups. Scale varies from 0.1 to 0.25 so the field has depth and size variation without a few large particles dominating.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/spheres.js#L25)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        rate: 12,
        radialSpeed: 1,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [6, 12],
          speed: 1,
          color: colors,
          scale: [
            new THREE.Vector3(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
            new THREE.Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
          ],
          alpha: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

The module collection is explicitly empty. Position changes come from the emitter’s initial velocity and system integration. Color, alpha, and size remain at their initial values, making this a useful baseline for checking the renderer before adding lifetime modifiers.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/spheres.js#L44)

```js
    modules: [],
```


## Renderers

A Circle sprite with lit material, spherical normals 1, and normal lighting 1 simulates rounded lighting on a flat billboard. Roughness 0.5 provides a softer surface response. The particles look volumetric without the vertex cost of one sphere mesh per particle.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/spheres.js#L48)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',

        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
          normalLighting: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],
```

# Stylized Depth

Depth-based color, scale, speed, rotation, and velocity modules for stylized perspective effects.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Stylized%20Depth)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Stylized Depth](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/stylizedDepth.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The system is offset to z=-6, with a 14-second loop and prewarm at 30 fps in the demo. Gravity is disabled so depth-dependent modules control motion. The broad initial volume supplies particles at many camera depths, making the styling differences visible at once.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/stylizedDepth.js#L19)

```js
  const system = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 14,
    prewarm: true,
    prewarmFPS: 30,
    looping: true,
    gravity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
    gravityModifier: 0,

    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.BoxGeometry(20, 10, 20),
        }),
        rate: 200,
        radialSpeed: 0,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [7, 12],
          speed: 1,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0.01, 0.02, 0.3),
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.02, 0.02, 0.02),
        },
      }),
    ],

    modules: [
      new ColorByDepth({
        color: [new THREE.Color('#fff7db'), new THREE.Color('#84d7ff')],
        alpha: [1, 0.5],
        depthRange,
      }),
      new ScaleByDepth({
        scale: [new THREE.Vector3(1, 1, 1), new THREE.Vector3(2, 2, 2)],
        depthRange,
      }),
      new RotationByDepth({
        angularVelocity: (t) => new THREE.Vector3(
          THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.12, 1.6, THREE.MathUtils.smoothstep(t, 0.15, 1)),
          0,
          0,
        ),
        depthRange,
      }),
      new VelocityByDepth({
        velocity: (t) => new THREE.Vector3(
          Math.sin(t * Math.PI * 2) * 0.08,
          THREE.MathUtils.lerp(-1, 1, t),
          THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0, 1, t),
        ),
        depthRange,
      }),
      new SpeedByDepth({
        speed: (t) => THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.5, 3, THREE.MathUtils.smoothstep(t, 0, 1)),
        depthRange,
      }),
    ],

    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'unlit',
        sizeAttenuation: false,
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

A 20×10×20 box emits 200 particles per second with lifetimes 7–12 seconds. Radial speed zero avoids a central explosion; velocity (0.01, 0.02, 0.3) creates a slow baseline drift. Initial scale 0.02 suits the renderer’s screen-oriented size configuration.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/stylizedDepth.js#L28)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: new THREE.BoxGeometry(20, 10, 20),
        }),
        rate: 200,
        radialSpeed: 0,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [7, 12],
          speed: 1,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0.01, 0.02, 0.3),
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.02, 0.02, 0.02),
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

All five modules share depthRange [5, 24]. Distant particles shift from warm white toward cyan and alpha 0.5 while scale increases up to 2. Rotation grows from 0.12 to 1.6, and velocity and speed vary with normalized depth. These are camera-depth responses, so moving the camera can change appearance without changing particle age.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/stylizedDepth.js#L46)

```js
    modules: [
      new ColorByDepth({
        color: [new THREE.Color('#fff7db'), new THREE.Color('#84d7ff')],
        alpha: [1, 0.5],
        depthRange,
      }),
      new ScaleByDepth({
        scale: [new THREE.Vector3(1, 1, 1), new THREE.Vector3(2, 2, 2)],
        depthRange,
      }),
      new RotationByDepth({
        angularVelocity: (t) => new THREE.Vector3(
          THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.12, 1.6, THREE.MathUtils.smoothstep(t, 0.15, 1)),
          0,
          0,
        ),
        depthRange,
      }),
      new VelocityByDepth({
        velocity: (t) => new THREE.Vector3(
          Math.sin(t * Math.PI * 2) * 0.08,
          THREE.MathUtils.lerp(-1, 1, t),
          THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0, 1, t),
        ),
        depthRange,
      }),
      new SpeedByDepth({
        speed: (t) => THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.5, 3, THREE.MathUtils.smoothstep(t, 0, 1)),
        depthRange,
      }),
    ],
```


## Renderers

Unlit Circle sprites keep color differences independent of scene lighting. sizeAttenuation false suppresses ordinary perspective size falloff, allowing ScaleByDepth to provide the deliberate depth styling. Compare screenshots with a consistent camera to avoid mistaking camera changes for simulation differences.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/stylizedDepth.js#L80)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'unlit',
        sizeAttenuation: false,
      }),
    ],
```

# Suzanne

Mesh-surface emission from a model with lit sprite rendering.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Suzanne)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Suzanne](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/suzanne.png)

## Particle System Configuration

This continuously looping 10-second system emits from a loaded model. Geometry is cloned before transformation so the GLTF asset’s original mesh is not modified. The source applies rotateX(-90), which Three.js interprets in radians; this documents the current transform rather than assuming it means a quarter-turn.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanne.js#L34)

```js
  const suzanne = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: suzanneGeometry,
          source: EmissionSource.Surface
        }),
        rate: 256,
        radialSpeed: 1.1,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 2.2,
          speed: 0,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.1125, 0.1125, 0.1125),
          color: new THREE.Color('#70d6ff'),
          alpha: 0.85,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
    modules: [
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#70d6ff'),
        alpha: (time) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(time, 0, 1))),
      }),
    ],
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

EmissionSource.Surface samples Suzanne’s geometry at 256 particles per second. Lifetime 2.2 gives roughly 563 visible particles before culling, enough to outline the model. Initial speed and velocity are zero, while radial speed 1.1 supplies source-directed motion; small scale 0.1125 keeps the sampled shape legible.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanne.js#L38)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        source: new EmissionShape({
          geometry: suzanneGeometry,
          source: EmissionSource.Surface
        }),
        rate: 256,
        radialSpeed: 1.1,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: 2.2,
          speed: 0,
          scale: new THREE.Vector3(0.1125, 0.1125, 0.1125),
          color: new THREE.Color('#70d6ff'),
          alpha: 0.85,
          velocity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

The color module keeps the cyan tint and applies a cubic alpha fade. Late fading preserves a recognizable shell for most of each particle’s life, then reduces visible popping as particles expire. No additional noise or force module obscures the model-based emission pattern.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanne.js#L58)

```js
    modules: [
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        color: new THREE.Color('#70d6ff'),
        alpha: (time) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(time, 0, 1))),
      }),
    ],
```


## Renderers

Circle sprites with lit material render each sample without instancing the entire Suzanne mesh per particle. The model is only the emission source. This makes the surface sampling easy to see while avoiding a scene filled with hundreds of full model instances.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanne.js#L66)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',
      }),
    ],
```

<!-- Source: apps/docs/examples/suzanneInstances.md -->


# Suzanne Instances

Mesh instancing with Suzanne particles and randomized transforms.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Suzanne%20Instances)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Suzanne Instances](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/suzanneInstances.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The 10-second loop and zero gravity keep the instanced models floating. GLTF geometry is cloned once and shared by the renderer. The existing rotateX(-90) call uses radians, so inspect the current orientation in a preview if changing the imported model.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanneInstances.js#L37)

```js
  const system = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    gravity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
    gravityModifier: 0,

    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        rate: 12,
        radialSpeed: 1,
        alignment: 1,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [4, 8],
          speed: 1,
          color: colors,
          scale: [
            new THREE.Vector3(0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
            new THREE.Vector3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
          ],
          alpha: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],

    modules: [
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (t) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(t, 0, 1)))
      })
    ],

    renderers: [
      new MeshRenderer({
        mesh: new THREE.Mesh(
          suzanneGeometry,
          new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial()
        ),
        castShadow: true,
        receiveShadow: true,
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

Rate 12, lifetimes 4–8 seconds, and scale 0.4–1 produce a manageable group of roughly 72 instances at average lifetime. Alignment 1 orients particles to emission direction. A four-color Set varies the instances without constructing a separate material for each particle.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanneInstances.js#L44)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        rate: 12,
        radialSpeed: 1,
        alignment: 1,
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [4, 8],
          speed: 1,
          color: colors,
          scale: [
            new THREE.Vector3(0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
            new THREE.Vector3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
          ],
          alpha: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

The sole ColorOverLifetime module applies a cubic alpha fade. It leaves scale and trajectory alone so the recognizable mesh silhouette and directional alignment carry the effect. Most of each lifetime remains visible before the late fade removes the instance.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanneInstances.js#L64)

```js
    modules: [
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (t) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(t, 0, 1)))
      })
    ],
```


## Renderers

MeshRenderer shares the loaded Suzanne geometry with a MeshStandardMaterial and enables cast/receive shadows. Unlike the Suzanne surface-emission example, every particle represents a full model. Watch geometry cost and draw workload when increasing the population.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/suzanneInstances.js#L72)

```js
    renderers: [
      new MeshRenderer({
        mesh: new THREE.Mesh(
          suzanneGeometry,
          new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial()
        ),
        castShadow: true,
        receiveShadow: true,
      }),
    ],
```

<!-- Source: apps/docs/examples/tags.md -->


# Cubes and Spheres

Tag-based module and renderer filtering by mixing cubes and spheres in one particle system.

[View live example](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/?preset=Cubes%20and%20Spheres)

Preset by [rzmay](https://github.com/rzmay).

![Generated preview of Cubes and Spheres](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/previews/tags.png)

## Particle System Configuration

The 10-second loop shares emission and zero-gravity integration between cubes and spheres. This demonstrates how one system can own several appearances without maintaining two independent simulations. Lifetimes 6–12 seconds leave time to compare the tagged behaviors.


[Source: system:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/tags.js#L24)

```js
  const system = new ParticleSystem({
    duration: 10,
    looping: true,
    gravity: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0),
    gravityModifier: 0,

    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        rate: 12,
        radialSpeed: 1,
        tags: ['spheres', 'cubes'],
        tagSelection: 'distribute',
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [6, 12],
          speed: 1,
          color: colors,
          scale: [
            new THREE.Vector3(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
            new THREE.Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
          ],
          alpha: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],

    modules: [
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: [new THREE.Vector3(5, 0, 1), new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, -5)],
        tags: 'cubes',
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (t) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(t, 0, 1))),
        tags: 'cubes',
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = (0.35 + (1.8 - 0.35) * time);
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
        tags: 'spheres'
      }),
      new Collision({ tags: 'spheres' })
    ],

    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',
        tags: 'spheres',
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
          normalLighting: 1,
        },
        castShadow: true,
      }),
      new MeshRenderer({
        tags: 'cubes',
        mesh: new THREE.Mesh(
          new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1),
          new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial()
        ),
        castShadow: true,
        receiveShadow: true,
      }),
    ],
  });
```


## Emitters

The emitter assigns spheres and cubes with tagSelection distribute, alternating groups instead of giving every particle both tags. Rate 12 means roughly six per second in each group. Scale 0.1–0.25 and a discrete four-color Set vary appearance while keeping particle motion comparable.


[Source: emitters:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/tags.js#L31)

```js
    emitters: [
      new Emitter({
        rate: 12,
        radialSpeed: 1,
        tags: ['spheres', 'cubes'],
        tagSelection: 'distribute',
        initialValues: {
          lifetime: [6, 12],
          speed: 1,
          color: colors,
          scale: [
            new THREE.Vector3(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
            new THREE.Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25),
          ],
          alpha: 1,
        },
      }),
    ],
```


## Modules

Only cubes receive rotation and cubic alpha fade. Only spheres receive growth from multiplier 0.35 to 1.8 and a Collision module. Matching tags on each module prevents accidental cross-group changes. Add collision scene geometry to see the sphere-only contact response.


[Source: modules:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/tags.js#L52)

```js
    modules: [
      new RotationOverLifetime({
        angularVelocity: [new THREE.Vector3(5, 0, 1), new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, -5)],
        tags: 'cubes',
      }),
      new ColorOverLifetime({
        alpha: (t) => (1 - Easing.cubic.in(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(t, 0, 1))),
        tags: 'cubes',
      }),
      new ScaleOverLifetime({
        scale: (time) => {
          const size = (0.35 + (1.8 - 0.35) * time);
          return new THREE.Vector3(size, size, size);
        },
        tags: 'spheres'
      }),
      new Collision({ tags: 'spheres' })
    ],
```


## Renderers

The sphere renderer filters to spheres and uses a lit Circle sprite with spherical normals. The cube renderer filters to cubes and instances BoxGeometry with MeshStandardMaterial. Both enable shadow casting, and cubes also receive shadows. Distributed tags avoid drawing both a mesh and a sprite for every particle.


[Source: renderers:1](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/blob/develop/examples/tags.js#L73)

```js
    renderers: [
      new SpriteRenderer(Textures.Circle, {
        material: 'lit',
        tags: 'spheres',
        materialOptions: {
          roughness: 0.5,
          sphericalNormals: 1,
          normalLighting: 1,
        },
        castShadow: true,
      }),
      new MeshRenderer({
        tags: 'cubes',
        mesh: new THREE.Mesh(
          new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1),
          new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial()
        ),
        castShadow: true,
        receiveShadow: true,
      }),
    ],
```

# AI Coding Assistants

The RZMPS skill helps coding assistants create and debug Three.js particle systems and VFX,
compose emitters, modules, spatial effects, and renderers, and validate WebGL and WebGPU
output using actual canvas previews. The complete skill lives in the public GitHub repository
at [.agents/skills/rzmps](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/tree/HEAD/.agents/skills/rzmps).
Its references are generated from these canonical human guides and API declarations.

## Installation

Choose an installation explicitly after reviewing the skill and authorizing any changes to
agent configuration. Installing `@rzmps/rzmps` with npm never installs a skill automatically.

<!-- distribution:installation:start -->
```bash
# Discover available skills
npx skills add rzmay/rzmps --list

# Install the RZMPS skill
npx skills add rzmay/rzmps --skill rzmps

# Install globally (optional)
npx skills add rzmay/rzmps --skill rzmps -g
```
<!-- distribution:installation:end -->

The CLI lets you select compatible agents. Project installation affects the current project;
`-g` installs at user scope. The skill follows the [Agent Skills format](https://agentskills.io/specification).
Compatible installers discover it directly from GitHub; no manual registry submission is required.
See the [skills CLI documentation](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) for agent selection and installation options.

These shorthand commands read the repository's default branch. They become available once
this skill is committed and published there. Before that, test the actual checkout with
`npx skills add . --list`, or use a published branch URL such as
`https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/tree/develop` in place of `rzmay/rzmps`.
Local validation does not prove that unpushed files are already discoverable from GitHub.

## Lightweight npm Guidance

<!-- distribution:npm-readme:start -->
The optional [RZMPS skill](https://github.com/rzmay/rzmps/tree/HEAD/.agents/skills/rzmps)
helps coding assistants build Three.js particle systems and VFX using emitters, modules,
renderers, and WebGL/WebGPU previews.

```bash
npx skills add rzmay/rzmps --skill rzmps
```

Review the skill and authorize installation before changing agent configuration.
The npm package includes a short generated `AGENTS.md`, without bundling the full skill or
its references. These entry points do not guarantee automatic agent discovery. For the
installed version's API, inspect `build/index.d.ts` and the package version; see the
[canonical documentation](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/) for guides.
<!-- distribution:npm-readme:end -->

## Discovery and Maintenance

The repository, this documentation site, the npm README, and generated `llms.txt` and
`llms-full.txt` all point to the same canonical skill. The site also exposes a generated
portable copy at [agent-skill/SKILL.md](https://rzmps.rzmay.com/docs/agent-skill/SKILL.md), with its relative references
alongside it. That hosted copy is generated, never independently maintained.

`npm run docs:generate` refreshes agent references, hosted skill files, npm `AGENTS.md`,
and README guidance blocks. `npm run agents:check` validates frontmatter and reference links,
discovers and installs the checkout skill in a temporary project, and audits `npm pack --dry-run`.
It leaves consumer projects and the user's agent configuration untouched.

Run `npm run agents:check -- --github` to test the exact public shorthand discovery command.
CI checks GitHub commit URLs after pushes and the shorthand after publishing to the default
branch; pull requests validate their checkout without assuming the proposed skill is already public.
